attributes.context: Article 26 defines “new technology” as the introduction of automated manufacturing machines, robots, computer-aided manufacturing systems, and other significant technology implementations that cause the direct elimination of work previously performed by represented employees.

extraction_text: 26.01(b) An employee directly affected by “new technology” as defined above will be offered retraining preference for a job for which the Company foresees a requirement, provided that equivalent job opportunities are not available and that they have the basic knowledge for the retraining.

attributes.context: The preceding Article 26 text defines “new technology” and provides that employees directly affected by it will be offered retraining preference.

extraction_text: 26.02 The Company will provide in written notification to the Union Business Representative or his designee of the Company's plans for the introduction of new technology, which may affect the employees. This notification will inform the Union of the anticipated schedules of the introduction of new technology and will identify areas of skill impacts and any training programs associated with those impacts.

attributes.context: It appears under ARTICLE 26 – NEW TECHNOLOGY, identifying the subject as new technology.

The same chunk also defines “new technology” as automated manufacturing machines, robots, computer-aided manufacturing systems, and other significant technology implementations that cause direct elimination of represented work, and provides for retraining preference and written union notification related to new technology introductions.

extraction_text: It is the Company's contemporary policy when possible, to assure that training is available for its employees so that they may have the opportunity to acquire the knowledge and skills required by the introduction of new technology.

attributes.context: The chunk’s preceding subsection (a) defines “new technology” as automated manufacturing machines, robots, computer-aided manufacturing systems, and other significant technology implementations that cause direct elimination of work performed by represented employees; it also states a company policy to make training available and requires written union notification of new technology plans.
